source: Albert Camus, The Rebel, Part One, The Rebel (trans. Anthony Bower, 1953)

evidence.where: Anthony Bower’s translation as quoted in a chapter-by-chapter reading of Part One (Vintage edition, p. 22) and in Wikiquote; the passage ends the chapter The Rebel with the cogito comparison and this sentence. The Internet Archive copies of the 1954 Knopf edition are lending-locked, so the page itself was not opened
evidence.locator: Part One, The Rebel, closing paragraph

reason: Bower’s rendering of Je me révolte, donc nous sommes closes Part One in exactly this wording; the sentence recurs in Part Five, but Part One is its first and defining statement. Camus has one January line, so the year count stays under the cap.
